 Appearance:
 MR K B MAGHNANI(9673) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR VICKY B MEHTA(5422) for the Applicant(s) No. 1  MR HARDIK SONI, APP for the Respondent(s) No. 1  ==========================================================

sentences.text:
By way of the present application under Section 482 of the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), the applicant-accused has prayed for enlarging the Applicant on anticipatory bail in connection with the F I R be i ng C. R. No . P a r t - A 1 1 8 2 2 0 1 9 2 4 0 9 7 6 o f 2 0 2 4 registered wit h Navsari Town Police Station, Navsari for the offe nce s puni sha bl e unde r S ec tions 465, 420,
467, 468, 471 and 114 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. Heard learned Advocate for the Applicant and learned APP for the Respondent - State.
2.1 Rule.
Learned APP waives service of Rule on behalf of the Respondent State.

sentences.text: Learned Advocate for the Applicant has submitted that the Applicant is apprehending arrest in connection the aforesaid FIR and in this NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19762/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined connection the earlier application filed by the Applicant before the learned Sessions Court came to be dis-allowed.
He submitted that considering the facts stated in the Application, the applicant may be granted anticipatory bail.
4. Learned Additional Public Prosecutor appearing on behalf of the respondent - State has opposed grant of anticipatory bail looking to the nature and gravity of the offence.
He submitted that an account was opened in the name of the first informant and a distributorship was obtained on the basis of the said account.
The signatures of the first informant was not found on the account opening form.
Thus, there is a reason to believe that the signatures of the first informant were forged on the said documents.
Learned APP has therefore prayed that the present Application may be dismissed.
5. Heard learned Advocates for the parties and perused the record.
At the outset, it is required to be noted that the alleged incident had taken place between 10.10.2008 to 31.3.2017, whereas the FIR came to be lodged in the year 2024.
In the interregnum the first informant appears to have lodged an application with the concerned police station.

However, after lodging the said application with the concerned police station, the first informant had given a statement before the concerned police authorities that he did not want to implicate the present applicant as an accused in the said complaint.
Therefore it was sought that the name of the present applicant to be deleted from the array of the accused persons in the application given by the first informant before the police authorities.
Moreover, the delay caused in lodging the FIR has not been satisfactorily explained.
Considering the same, the present Application deserves to be allowed.

6. Having heard the arguments advanced by the learned advocates NEUTRAL CITATION R/CR.MA/19762/2024 ORDER DATED: 09/10/2024 undefined for the parties and perusing the material placed on record and taking into consideration the facts of the case, nature of allegations,
gravity of offence and the role attributed to the accused, I am inclined to grant anticipatory bail to the applicant.
Therefore, in the facts and circumstances of the present case, this court is inclined to consider the case of the applicant.

9.

The applicant is ordered to be released on anticipatory bail in the event of arrest in connection with a F I R be i ng C. R. No .
